title: The Two Dervishes at the City Gate (ML)
summary: Two travelers ask about the people of Agra before entering. Birbal gives both opposite answers, revealing a profound psychological truth.
full_text:
One afternoon, Birbal was sitting quietly in the shade of the archway at the western gate of Agra when a traveling dervish arrived, dusty and tired from a long journey.

The traveler stopped and asked Birbal: 'Friend, I am new to this province. Tell me—what kind of people live in this city of Agra? Are they kind and welcoming, or cruel and treacherous?'

Birbal looked at the traveler and asked: 'Tell me, brother—what kind of people lived in the city from which you have just traveled?'

The traveler scowled: 'Oh, they were horrible! Selfish, greedy, dishonest, and constantly backbiting! I could not wait to leave them behind!'

Birbal sighed: 'Alas, my friend. I fear you will find the people of Agra to be exactly the same—selfish, greedy, and untrustworthy.'

The traveler sighed in disappointment and entered the city gates.

An hour later, a second traveling dervish approached the same gate. He stopped, greeted Birbal with a warm smile, and asked: 'Peace be upon you, sir. I am entering Agra for the first time. Can you tell me what kind of people dwell in this city?'

Birbal asked again: 'Brother, what kind of people lived in the town you have just left?'

The second traveler's face lit up with affection: 'Ah, they were wonderful! Generous, honest, hospitable, and always ready to help a neighbor in need. My heart was broken to part from them!'

Birbal smiled warmly: 'Rejoice, my friend! You will find the people of Agra to be exactly the same—kind, generous, honest, and welcoming!'

An imperial guard standing nearby had overheard both conversations and was completely bewildered: 'Raja Birbal! Why did you tell the first traveler that Agra is full of wicked scoundrels, and the second traveler that Agra is full of saints?'

Birbal explained with profound simplicity:

'Because, my friend, we do not see the world as it is; we see the world as WE are!

'A suspicious, bitter man carries suspicion in his heart, and will provoke selfishness in everyone he meets. A generous, loving man carries warmth in his heart, and will awaken kindness wherever he walks. The world is merely a mirror reflecting our own inner character.'

The guard bowed in deep reverence at Birbal's wisdom.
